description: Team Xcrew is a beginner-friendly team that welcomes curious minds with a passion for space and a willingness to learn and create together. No prior experience is required. We are seeking three teammates to contribute to game logic, design, and research.
summary:
Tradespace is an interactive web app that teaches the trade-offs behind real space missions. Every rocket is a compromise between thrust, fuel, cost and payload, but that is hard to see from a finished launch. Tradespace lets anyone make those choices and see the results.

Players start in the Mission Builder, where they pick a vehicle and destination and configure the engine, fuel, boosters and payload. In the Rocket Garage they customize the rocket, with a live preview and a model of NASA’s SLS for comparison. Then they launch in 3D and fly to Earth orbit or the Moon, with Earth and Moon rendered from NASA imagery.

After each mission, a report explains in plain language what the design did well and what a different choice would have changed. A design-space plot shows where the design sits among the alternatives. A leaderboard and achievements encourage players to try again and improve.

Tradespace helps students and the public learn how engineers think, and gives teachers a hands-on way to set challenges. It runs in the browser with nothing to install.

Built with React, TypeScript, Vite and three.js, using NASA imagery, and developed by a team working on separate branches that we merged into one project.
details:
Tradespace is a web app where you design a space mission, launch it in 3D and see how your choices played out. You choose a vehicle and destination in the Mission Builder, customize the rocket in the Rocket Garage, then fly it to orbit or the Moon. A mission report and a design-space plot show what your design did well and how it compares to the alternatives.

Benefits:
It makes engineering trade-offs visible and interactive. It runs in the browser with nothing to install.

Intended impact:
Help students and the public understand why real missions are compromises, and give teachers a hands-on way to set challenges.

Tools and technologies:
React, TypeScript, Vite, three.js, Git and GitHub. Earth and Moon textures from NASA imagery.

Creativity:
We turned abstract trade-off analysis into a game with a rocket garage, 3D launches, a plain-language report, a leaderboard and achievements.

Factors we considered:
Ease of use for beginners, scientific accuracy, performance in the browser, and the chance to learn by trying again.
